I am 72 years old this year, and I have been farming this 1.2 mu of land for 40 years. I only went to middle school, but I know my own land like the back of my hand. My neighbor Lao Wang and I have land right next to each other, and we usually do about the same thing.

This land is all I have. At my age, I work alone. My nephew helps for a day or two during harvest, but mostly it is just me. So I cannot mess around with fancy new methods. I stick with what works.

**Wheat (this winter):**
I plant wheat right after the National Day holiday, around October 8th. I use the same improved variety I have been using — it is called Jimai 22, or something like that. The seed dealer says there are newer kinds, but this one has given me 500 jin per mu reliably, so why change? I buy 15 jin of seed for the 1.2 mu. 

For fertilizer, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer (40 kg, 15-15-15) as base fertilizer when I till the land. That is about 5 kg each of N, P, and K per mu. Then at green-up time in March, I spread 25 kg of urea (46% nitrogen) — that gives another 9-10 kg of nitrogen per mu. Some years I add a little more if the wheat looks yellow. I would rather spend the extra 20 yuan than lose yield. I do not bother with separate phosphorus or potassium topdressing. The compound fertilizer has some, and that is enough.

I irrigate three times: once at green-up/jointing in late March, once at heading in late April, and once during grain filling in mid-May. My well works fine. Electricity costs money, but three times is what this land needs. I till with the rotary tiller before planting — not deep ploughing, just rotary. It is faster and easier on my back.

For pests, I spray herbicide once in early spring, and if there are aphids or rust that year, I spray once more. Last year I sprayed twice, so this year I plan for two times.

I expect about 500 kg per mu. On a good year I get a bit more, but at my age I do not push too hard.

**Maize (next summer):**
As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I plant maize. Everyone here uses hybrid seed — you cannot get good yield without it. I buy 3 jin of hybrid seed. I do not till again after wheat. There is no time, and the wheat stubble helps keep moisture. I use the no-till planter.

For fertilizer, I put down 25 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) at planting — that is about 3 kg each per mu in the row. Then I topdress with 40 kg of urea when the maize is at the big trumpet stage. That gives about 15 kg nitrogen per mu total. So altogether about 18 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu.

I irrigate three times: once as seedlings if it is dry in June, once at the big trumpet stage in July, and once at filling in August. The summer rain helps, but you cannot rely on it.

Pesticide: I spray herbicide right after planting, and I spray for corn borer once in July. Two times total.

I expect about 550 kg per mu. That is what I usually get if the weather is normal.

Why these numbers? Because this is what I did last year, and last year was fine. Lao Wang does about the same. I spend roughly 300 yuan on fertilizer and seed for wheat, and 280 yuan for maize. If I cut back, I might save 50 yuan but lose 100 kg of grain. That is stupid. But I also do not put on more than this — extra fertilizer just wastes money on such a small plot.
